name: TN-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a PVI of R+17
Incumbent Tim Burchett running for reelection with a large fundraising edge
No general-election polling and no expert ratings, leaving fundamentals as the main guide
Prediction markets price the Democrat at only about 4%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Republican incumbent Tim Burchett: the district leans R+17, he holds a roughly six-to-one fundraising advantage over Michaela Barnett, and markets give the Democrat only a small chance. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict that picture, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Barnett within single digits, or significant outside spending entering the district, would be the first sign this is more competitive than the fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tim Burchett, the Republican incumbent, is seeking another term in a Knoxville-area district that leans heavily Republican, with a partisan baseline of R+17. He has raised about $2.4 million and holds nearly $1 million on hand, while Democrat Michaela Barnett has raised roughly $400,000 with modest cash remaining and no outside spending on either side. No independent candidates are seen as factors.

There is no public general-election polling and no expert ratings for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency advantage, and the money gap. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 4% chance of an upset, consistent with a comfortable Republican win.
